correctness.rationale: The exact beta/hypergeometric identity Th=AgF(r²)/F(1) has both numerator parameters <0, positive denominator and convergence excess >0; strict monotonicity gives a strictly positive interior Schur gap. The published independent dual bound T*g≤Bh with AB=C* and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz give a nonnegative defect represented as a kernel integral. The elementary uniform bound on |r|≤1/2 and exact cap geometry yield the stated κ(δ)>0 for all n≥2, α>max(−1,−(n−1)/2), δ∈(0,1]. No compactness assumption is hidden, and limit corollaries follow by domination and σ({±η})=0. The included numerical checker tests scalar identities but is not used as proof.

value.rationale: A sharp trace norm alone does not describe loss of compactness. The uniform positive explicit κ(δ) proves that every near-extremizer has boundary L² mass concentrated in neighborhoods of exactly the two geometric endpoints, ruling out every off-pole loss mechanism for an infinite family of dimensions and invariant Laplacian parameters. This is a parameter-uniform structural stability theorem tied to the existing sharpness construction, not a normalization test or a merely numerical improvement.
